rules.normalizedProposition: A Nevada motor-vehicle owner subject to NRS 485.185 must continuously maintain at least $25,000 of liability coverage for bodily injury to or death of one person in one crash.
rules.applicability: Owners of motor vehicles registered or required to be registered in Nevada while the vehicle is present or registered in Nevada.
exceptions: Mopeds are excluded by NRS 485.185(2).
rules.supersessionCheck: Current official NRS chapter captured October 7, 2026; SB 308 effective-date clause checked in official 2017 Statutes.

rules.normalizedProposition: Subject to the per-person limit, a Nevada motor-vehicle owner subject to NRS 485.185 must continuously maintain at least $50,000 of liability coverage for bodily injury to or death of two or more persons in one crash.
rules.applicability: Same as NV-MINIMUM-LIABILITY-001.
exceptions: Mopeds are excluded by NRS 485.185(2).
rules.supersessionCheck: Same current-code and effective-date review as rule 001.

rules.normalizedProposition: A Nevada motor-vehicle owner subject to NRS 485.185 must continuously maintain at least $20,000 of liability coverage for injury to or destruction of others' property in one crash.
rules.applicability: Same as NV-MINIMUM-LIABILITY-001.
exceptions: Mopeds are excluded by NRS 485.185(2).
rules.supersessionCheck: Same current-code and effective-date review as rule 001.

rules.normalizedProposition: A Nevada motor-vehicle liability policy must include uninsured-vehicle bodily-injury coverage at no less than Chapter 485 bodily-injury minimums unless a named insured rejects it in writing on an insurer-furnished form describing the rejected coverage; renewal does not require the coverage unless the named insured requests it in writing.
rules.applicability: Policies delivered or issued for delivery in Nevada insuring motor-vehicle ownership, maintenance, or use.
exceptions: State of Nevada and political-subdivision policies
Written rejection by a named insured
NRS 690B.035 damage-only operator policy
requiredEvidence: UM coverage and limits, or written insurer-form rejection by a named insured
openQuestions: Independent verifier must confirm the effective date applicable to the captured current text and whether a particular carrier form becomes proposition-dependent evidence.

rules.normalizedProposition: Nevada evidence of motor-vehicle insurance must be on a Commissioner-approved form and include the policyholder and insurer names and addresses, specified vehicle identification, policy effective and expiration dates, policy number, a statement of compliance with NRS 485.185, and the prescribed carry-in-vehicle statement.
rules.applicability: Insurers providing insurance required by NRS 485.185 through an insurance contract.
exceptions: NRS 690B.023(2) allows an approved electronic format on insured request, while retaining the same information requirements.
requiredEvidence: Vehicle year/make/VIN or qualifying fleet designation
openQuestions: Exact effective date for the current consolidated text requires verifier confirmation.

rules.normalizedProposition: A person may not sell, solicit, or negotiate a class of insurance in Nevada unless licensed for that class; an insurer's producer-license exemption does not extend to officers, directors, employees, subsidiaries, or affiliates that perform those activities.
rules.applicability: Persons selling, soliciting, or negotiating personal-auto insurance in Nevada.
exceptions: Insurer itself
Applicable exemptions in NRS 683A.211, only within their stated limits
openQuestions: The exact accepted Nevada license-class mapping, business-entity requirement, and appointment requirement require verifier confirmation against NRS 683A.261-.321 and current DOI operational records.

rules.normalizedProposition: An insurer or producer may pay compensation to a person who does not sell, solicit, or negotiate insurance in Nevada unless the payment violates NRS 686A.110 or 686A.120; compensation for licensable selling, solicitation, or negotiation may not be paid to or accepted by an unlicensed person.
rules.applicability: Provider-paid Open Polici compensation associated with Nevada opportunities.
exceptions: The statutory permission does not protect conduct that is actually selling, soliciting, or negotiating
Property/casualty inducement restrictions require separate review under NRS 686A.130
openQuestions: A qualified independent verifier must determine whether each comparison and explanation function remains outside sell, solicit, and negotiate; software cannot resolve that legal characterization.

rules.normalizedProposition: Except for statutory exceptions, a property or casualty insurer or its representative, broker, agent, or solicitor may not provide an unfiled premium rebate, discount, credit, special policy benefit, or valuable inducement to insurance.
rules.applicability: Nevada property and casualty insurance, including personal auto.
exceptions: Items permitted by subsection 2 up to the statutory aggregate limit
Benefits or consideration specified in the policy or applicable filing
Other exceptions stated in NRS 686A.130
requiredEvidence: Annual aggregate-value evidence where an exception is invoked
openQuestions: Verifier must confirm the current effective date and treatment of any Open Polici consumer benefit before this becomes executable.

rules.normalizedProposition: A Nevada insurance producer acting as an insurer's agent must be appointed by that insurer; a producer not acting as an agent is a broker and does not require appointment, subject to the placement restriction in NRS 683A.321(5).
rules.applicability: Nevada personal-auto producers acting as agents of insurers and brokers placing Nevada risks.
exceptions: A producer acting as a broker does not require appointment under subsection 1.
The NRS 691E.210 exception and the placement categories in subsection 5 require transaction-specific review.
requiredEvidence: Current appointment when acting as agent
Authorized-insurer relationship when placement is through a broker
openQuestions: The effective period of the current consolidated text and the operational source used to prove appointment status require independent verification.

rules.normalizedProposition: Except for transactions expressly exempted by the Nevada Insurance Code, a person may not act as an insurer and an insurer may not transact insurance in Nevada unless the Commissioner has issued a certificate of authority that remains in force.
rules.applicability: Insurers whose Nevada personal-auto offers or policies are presented through Open Polici.
exceptions: Transactions expressly exempted by the Nevada Insurance Code, including applicable NRS 680A.070 exceptions.
openQuestions: The authoritative operational lookup and exact line-of-business mapping must be identified and independently verified before this can be executable.

rules.normalizedProposition: A Nevada insurance binder may be issued only by a resident or nonresident agent appointed by the insurer that will issue the policy and, absent the Commissioner's written approval for 30-day extensions, may not remain effective for more than 90 days.
rules.applicability: Binders associated with Nevada insurance transactions, including personal auto.
exceptions: The Commissioner may approve 30-day extensions in writing.
Any additional statutory exception must be evaluated from the full binder provisions.
requiredEvidence: Commissioner extension approval if duration exceeds 90 days
Approved binder form and delivery evidence if written
openQuestions: The platform does not issue binders; verifier must confirm whether this operates only as a provider-reported reconciliation control and whether form approval evidence is proposition-dependent.

rules.normalizedProposition: A notice required by NRS 687B.320 through 687B.350 must be personally delivered or mailed first class or certified to the insured's last known address, state the effective date of cancellation or nonrenewal, and include a written explanation of the specific reasons.
rules.applicability: Cancellation and nonrenewal notices governed by NRS 687B.320 through 687B.350, including applicable personal-auto policies.
exceptions: Applicability, grounds, and timing vary by cancellation or nonrenewal type and must be determined under the referenced sections.
openQuestions: This candidate captures common delivery and content only; separate atomic rules for grounds and timing under NRS 687B.320, .330, .340 and .350 remain to be extracted.

rules.normalizedProposition: Nevada's personal-lines producer authority includes automobile and motorcycle insurance; property and casualty are also separately recognized producer lines of authority, so a producer handling personal auto must hold a current license with an applicable authority for the transaction.
rules.applicability: Natural-person and business-organization producers participating in Nevada personal-auto transactions.
exceptions: The precise authority sufficient for a particular role may depend on whether the producer holds personal-lines authority or the relevant property/casualty authorities.
requiredEvidence: Active line or lines of authority
openQuestions: Independent verification must resolve whether property and casualty must both be held for each personal-auto activity and normalize current DOI authority codes.

rules.normalizedProposition: A business organization must be licensed as a Nevada producer of insurance to act as a producer and must designate a licensed natural person authorized to transact for the organization as responsible for its Nevada insurance-law compliance.
rules.applicability: Provider organizations acting as insurance producers in Nevada.
exceptions: Organizations that do not act as producers require separate classification; payment or platform enrollment does not establish an exemption.
openQuestions: Operational proof sources and the treatment of direct insurers versus producer organizations require independent verification.

rules.normalizedProposition: After a non-industrial insurance policy has been effective for at least 70 days or has been renewed, an insurer may cancel it before the earlier of the agreed term's expiration or one year from the effective date only for a ground listed in NRS 687B.320(1); cancellation requires at least 10 days' notice for nonpayment of premium and at least 30 days' notice for another listed ground.
rules.applicability: Non-industrial Nevada policies within the protected midterm period, including applicable personal-auto policies.
exceptions: Policies not yet effective for 70 days and not renewed
Industrial insurance policies
Cancellation after the protected period requires separate analysis
openQuestions: Each permissible statutory ground should be normalized separately before automated ground validation is considered.

rules.normalizedProposition: Unless an exception in NRS 687B.340(2) applies, a Nevada insurer must mail or deliver notice of intended nonrenewal at least 30 days before expiration for a noncommercial policy; failure to give timely notice requires an identical-terms replacement policy for the statutory renewal period.
rules.applicability: Nevada personal-auto policies not classified as commercial or business policies.
exceptions: Policyholder accepted replacement coverage
Policyholder requested or agreed to nonrenewal
Policy expressly designated nonrenewable by an approved or deemed-approved clause
openQuestions: Verifier must confirm date-counting convention and evidence sufficient to establish each exception.

rules.normalizedProposition: Unless an exception in NRS 687B.350(2) or (3) applies, an insurer renewing a Nevada policy with changed policy or coverage provisions, including changed rates or premiums, must notify the insured in writing at least 30 days before expiration; inadequate or untimely notice requires renewal under the expiring provisions for the statutory renewal period.
rules.applicability: Renewals of Nevada policies with changes in policy or coverage provisions.
exceptions: Specified industrial-insurance rate changes
Premium decrease only
Effective/expiration date change with unchanged duration only
Coverage-condition change favorable to insured without an accompanying less-favorable change
openQuestions: Verifier must confirm date counting and how compound favorable/unfavorable changes are classified.

rules.normalizedProposition: A Nevada insurance institution or agent must provide applicants and policyholders a written notice explaining its information-gathering practices at the time prescribed by NAC 679B.685 and containing the categories, disclosure circumstances, and access-and-correction rights specified there.
rules.applicability: Nevada insurance institutions and agents gathering personal information in connection with insurance applications, renewals, reinstatements, or benefit changes.
exceptions: Timing and whether notice is required vary with the information sources and prior notice history.
Another authorized insurance institution or agent may satisfy the obligation on behalf of the responsible party.
openQuestions: Open Polici's classification under these regulations and the allocation of notice responsibility among platform, agent and insurer require independent legal verification.

rules.normalizedProposition: A disclosure authorization used by a Nevada insurance institution, agent, or insurance-support organization in an insurance transaction must use plain language, be dated, identify the discloser, information, recipient, purpose and duration, and include the natural person's signature; for property or casualty application, reinstatement, or benefit-change information, the authorization may remain valid no longer than one year from signature.
rules.applicability: Personal or privileged information authorization forms used in Nevada insurance transactions by a regulated institution, agent, or insurance-support organization.
exceptions: Claim-related authorizations and life, health, or disability authorizations have different duration provisions.
openQuestions: The full subsection text and electronic-signature interaction must be independently verified before automated enforcement.

rules.normalizedProposition: A Nevada policy issued to replace a binder must carry coverage limits equal to the binder's limits and the same effective date as the initial binder; its premium must include the binder period at rates filed with the Commissioner.
rules.applicability: Nevada policies issued to replace insurance binders.
requiredEvidence: Binder coverage limits and effective date
Issued-policy coverage limits and effective date
openQuestions: Filed-rate evidence and any later specific personal-auto provisions require independent verification.
